prompt:
Create one finished, flat, opaque landscape 16:9 event poster for subway-station and neighborhood-community digital screens. It announces an outdoor short-film screening and a conversation with directors, welcoming local adults. Use a graphic architectural illustration with a continuous oblique-overhead riverbank environment and distributed, flat horizontal editorial typography. This is an evocative invented site drawing, not a surveyed reconstruction. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

WHOLE VISUAL CONSTRUCTION
The picture is a single connected place: a dark teal river winds from the top near the center diagonally toward the lower-left edge, continuing out of both edges. Warm apricot dry banks flank it. A long pale coral pedestrian bridge crosses the upper-middle at a shallow diagonal, its deck, railings, visible side face and piers sharing a coherent oblique projection. The piers visibly support the deck; the deck crosses water and joins both banks. The sheltered screening nook sits on the left/middle dry bank beneath the bridge's left end, with a pale upright cinema screen facing seated adult neighbors on several clearly supported patterned mats. Give the screen a simple wordless cinematic scene: one dark tree silhouette and warm moon on a deep blue rectangle, not writing or a blank bulletin board. Small projector on a stable stand points toward the screen. Show a restrained group of 7–9 adults in varied casual winter layers, with recognizable seated poses and feet/legs supported by mats. Keep head/body/limb ownership clear in the overhead drawing.

On the right bank, beyond the bridge, depict a visible conversation cluster: a standing adult speaker holds a dark microphone with one clearly connected bent arm and hand, facing 4–5 attentive adults seated on simple chairs in a loose semicircle. Each chair supports its person, with coherent seat/back/leg connections. A gently curving unlabelled path connects the right entrance, this cluster and the screening nook through the bank; the river, bridge, mats, speaker and circulation carry the main visual idea. Do not substitute scattered isolated icons. Keep adults sociable and natural, not children or toy figures.

COMPOSITION AND READING
Use the land clearings to protect text, with no text drawn on miniature objects, mats, bridge, water, or perspective planes. Coordinates below are approximate 1280x720 DESIGN proportions only; output is native maximum at 16:9.
Upper-left dry-bank clearing, about 470px wide, holds title, English, descriptor on a shared left alignment with generous margins. First sight is the identity against warm land; bridge and screening then lead the eye diagonally down to a broad lower-center bank clearing (430–490px usable width), where date, time and venue make the next useful reading group. A broad upper-right dry-bank entrance clearing (350–390px usable width) holds admission and capacity. A lower-right bank clearing holds mat and weather guidance, separated from the lower-center schedule by land/path and from the conversation by comfortable whitespace. These are local information pockets within one terrain, not a rigid sidebar, boxed column or full-width footer. Let illustration angles flow around the horizontal baseline groups. Ensure every group is comfortably inside the poster with clear spacing.

LETTERING AND EXACT PRINTED COPY
Render only these ten entries, each exactly once. Preserve every Hangul syllable, English case, digit, word space, middle dot, colon and the time-range en dash. No extra labels. Each of these entries stays on one horizontal line if possible; if truly needed, wrap only at an existing word boundary. Use friendly robust Korean sans with standard compact Hangul proportions, clean counters and steady stroke weights, dark navy on uninterrupted pale apricot ground. No expressive distortion. Title about 55 design px, English 28px, descriptor 31px. Date and time about 40px, venue 35px. All practical right-bank entries 32px with 335+px usable width. At a real 720px-wide view practical text must remain comfortably readable; enlarge clearings or reduce the bridge/image/title before shrinking facts. Maintain visible colon dot pairs, the horizontal range dash and optical middle dots with word gaps.

FINISH AND CONSTRAINTS
Bounded flat colors, navy drawing strokes with subtle consistent dry drawn edges, controlled hand-drawn rhythm, shallow oblique depth throughout. Dark teal water, apricot land, pale ivory screen, coral bridge and small muted blue/ochre seating accents. Avoid heavy noisy grain over text. Use few coherent ripple lines and ground contours tied to the terrain, not arbitrary decoration. Screen/mats/chairs stay on dry ground. Preserve the outdoor screening and microphone conversation as legible actions. Adult cultural-event tone: inviting and lively with controlled architectural detail. One standalone poster only, edge-to-edge opaque art; no panels, contact sheet, mockup, frame, visible tape, logos, QR, watermark, credits, pseudo-print, invented signs or added text.
